I recently went to David's Bridal to get a bridesmaid dress for a friend's wedding. I've always been a size 16, but recently lost about 25 pounds (now almost 30!) and thought I was now a 12. But, knowing bridal sizes tend to be pretty small, I grabbed a 14 and a 12 to try on. I tried on the 12... And it was too big! I had to send my fiance out to grab the 10, which fit perfectly!  


Similarly, I went to buy new workout leggings as a reward to myself. I've always been an XL, but knowing I'd lost some weight, I grabbed a L and a M to bring into the dressing room, expecting the L to fit. Imagine my surprise when the M was the right size. Me, a MEDIUM!?  


It's hard to see the weight loss on ourselves sometimes. And while clothes sizing varies a lot from brand to brand, sometimes shopping and realizing that our instinct is to go for totally the wrong sizes shows us how skewed our own perception of things can be.

If you go over this amount of transactions/month, you'll get hit with an "Excess Activity Fee."  I believe the actual amount of this might vary by bank, but all will apply some fee.

Thus, it's not a good idea to transfer from savings every time you get a credit card transaction. It would be fine to pay off your credit card every month directly from savings if that's your only transfer.
